$sources: NBCC 2020 4.1.6.2: S = Is [Ss (Cb Cw Cs Ca) + Sr]; Cb 0.8 (4.1.6.2(2)), Cw 1.0 or 0.75 / 0.5 for exposed roofs (4.1.6.2(3)), Cs by the slope (4.1.6.2(5)), Ca 1.0 (uniform load); Is of Table 4.1.6.2-A
source: NBCC 2020 4.1.6.2 (the uniform roof snow load; drifts, sliding and the other shape factors Ca are not covered)

sheltered.description: Roof not exposed to the wind (Cw = 1.0)

exposed.description: Roof fully exposed to the wind, Low and Normal importance (Cw = 0.75)

exposedNorth.description: Roof fully exposed to the wind, north of the tree line (Cw = 0.5)

sources.factor: NBCC 2020 4.1.6.2(2): the basic roof snow load factor Cb = 0.8 (roofs whose smaller plan dimension is small enough; larger roofs take a larger Cb: not covered)
sources.shape: NBCC 2020 4.1.6.2(5): the slope factor Cs = 1.0 up to 30°, linear to 0 at 70° (roofs other than unobstructed slippery roofs; those take 15° to 60°: not covered, on the safe side)
sources.exposures: NBCC 2020 4.1.6.2(3): the wind exposure factor Cw (in the program's Ce); 0.75 and 0.5 only for Low and Normal importance roofs fully exposed
sources.thermal: Ca = 1.0 (the uniform load; drifts and other accumulations not covered)
sources.importance: NBCC 2020 Table 4.1.6.2-A: IS (ULS) 0.8 Low, 1.0 Normal, 1.15 High, 1.25 Post-disaster
sources.loadCase: NBCC 2020 4.1.5.3 and 4.1.6: the roof takes the larger of the snow and the roof live load (case Lr, the envelope)
sources.rainShare: NBCC 2020 4.1.6.2(1): + Sr (the town's associated rain load) × Is
sources.seismicShare: NBCC 2020 4.1.8.2 (W): 25 % of the design snow load in the seismic weight
